summary: Walter Pater's first letter to Wilde, July 1877 — the only direct contact recorded here, kept because of what it was worth to Wilde.
certainty_reasoning: The record documents a friendship or acquaintance with no evidence of attraction or romance; classified platonic, upgradable if contrary evidence comes to light.

sources.quote:
Dear Mr Wilde, Accept my best thanks for the magazine and your letter. Your excellent article on the Grosvenor Gallery I read with very great pleasure; it makes me much wish to make your acquaintance, and I hope you will give me an early call on your return to Oxford.

I should much like to talk over some of the points with you, though on the whole I think your criticism very just, and it is certainly very pleasantly expressed. It shows that you possess some beautiful, and ~~at~~ for your age quite exceptionally cultivated, tastes; and a considerable knowledge also of many beautiful things. I hope you will write a great deal in time to come. Very truly yours

WALTER PATER
sources.context: Walter Pater to Oscar Wilde, headed 'Bradmore Road. Oxford. July 14' [1877], quoted whole from the autograph at the Ransom Center. Wilde had sent him the Dublin University Magazine carrying his notice of the Grosvenor Gallery's opening; this is the reply, and the beginning of the acquaintance. Wilde forwarded the letter to William Ward and asked for it back by registered post.
sources.speaker: Walter Pater
sources.supports: The first contact, in Pater's own hand, and what it was worth to Wilde.
sources.citation_provenance: PDF p. 86. The quotation follows the AUTOGRAPH, not the text printed there: the editors set this letter from Wilde's own copy of it inside his letter to Ward, and the two differ. See `original_provenance` for the variants.

facsimile.caption: Pater's two sides, headed Bradmore Road, Oxford, July 14 [1877]; the second sheet carries the whole of the second half and the signature. Wilde sent the original on to William Ward and asked for it back by registered post - his covering letter is at Magdalen, this is the enclosure

sources.original_provenance: Read at HRC MSS_WildeO_2_11_056 and _057, Pater's two sides in his own hand. One authorial cancellation, on _057: 'at' struck through and 'for' written above it on a caret, kept here as ~~at~~ for. NORMALISED: 'Gros-/venor' is broken by the line ending on _056 and is closed up, per the rule that marks produced by a line break alone are not preserved. VARIANTS from the printed text at PDF p. 86, all adopted here in the autograph's favour: manuscript 'pleasure;' for printed 'pleasure:'; 'your criticism very just, and it is certainly' for 'your criticisms very just, and they are certainly'; 'It shows' for 'The article shows'; 'knowledge also of' for 'knowledge too of'; 'cultivated, tastes;' for 'cultivated tastes:'. The printed readings are Wilde's transcription, not Pater's writing.
